An insurer holds $120M of interest-rate-sensitive bonds and $10M of cash against $100M of interest-rate-sensitive policy liabilities. Bond modified duration is 6 and liability modified duration is 3. Interest rates rise 125 bp; ignore convexity and use ΔV/V≈−DΔy for both assets and liabilities.


Immediately after repricing, policyholders surrender contracts requiring a $25M cash payment. Paying these surrenders simultaneously releases $25M of policy liabilities. The insurer must still hold at least $2M of cash after the payout. To fund the payout and cash floor, it sells bonds. Bonds are sold at a 3% discount to their already-stressed market value; the realized discount loss reduces own funds.


Base SCR is $20M. The market-rate stress increases SCR by 10%, and the lapse event increases the resulting SCR by a further 25% (apply the multipliers sequentially). The required solvency ratio is 100%.


Calculate stressed bond value and liabilities, own funds before lapses, the minimum bond amount sold at stressed market value, sale loss, post-lapse assets/liabilities/own funds, stressed SCR, solvency ratio, and minimum capital injection.


Assume any capital injection increases own funds dollar-for-dollar and does not change SCR.
